issues.title: Grenville's suggestion
issues.author: mohittahiliani
issues.body:
Grenville Armitage suggested the following alternative to the last paragraph of Section 1:

"An implementation of FQ-PIE has been incorporated into the mainline Linux kernel as a queuing discipline (qdisc) [LINUX-FQ-PIE] and is supported by several Linux distributions. Another implementation has also been incorporated into FreeBSD [FREEBSD-FQ-PIE]. Finally, an implementation of FQ-PIE is also available in  the ns-3 network simulator [ns-3-FQ-PIE]."

This is to make it clear that the Linux and FreeBSD implementations are independent, and ensure no-one accidentally assumes one is a port of the other.

issues.title: Suggestions from Chris - November 4 (IETF 124)
issues.author: mohittahiliani
issues.body:
Mailing list thread: https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/tsvwg/yIbAhtV0hUVbMjrUPCV2R6Pd9CA/

Section 4
I would prefer that RFC8033 (PIE) did not say the latency target "SHOULD be 15ms", as the optimum queue size depends very much on the variability of the bottleneck bandwidth. Constant bandwidth can handle a shorter standing queue. Wireless links often require a longer queue unless they are to sacrifice a lot of throughput. So for this draft I'd prefer that we didn't reinforce the problem. Instead of "(recommended as 15ms in RFC8033)" we could say "(such as the 15ms default in RFC8033)".

Section 4.1 Enqueue
This says "It is important to note that the timestamping approach provides a "per-packet queue delay," while the drop probability is calculated periodically (every 15 ms, as specified in [RFC8033]). Therefore, the FQ-PIE algorithm MAY use the queue delay value from the most recently dequeued packet when calculating the drop probability."
This feels like a big choice being offered to the implementer. Either we change the drop probability every packet, or we change it every 15ms. As all three current implementations take the per-packet approach, should we instead make this the default in the document? Are there some circumstances in which every 15ms is better? If yes, let's describe that. If not, get rid of it entirely.

"FQ-PIE does not adopt this approach for the reasons explained below."
I think the document would be easier to read if we move the reasons paragraph to an appendix.

Section 4.3 ECN Support
As L4S was published as RFC9330 nearly three years ago, any mention of ECN in this document shouldn't ignore its presence. These days ECT(1) does not generally imply classic 3168 marking.

RFC9330 section 4.2b actually mentions FQ-PIE!
"Per-Flow Queues and AQMs: A scheduler with per-flow queues, such as FQ-CoDel or FQ-PIE, can be used for L4S. For instance, within each queue of an FQ-CoDel system, as well as a CoDel AQM, there is typically also the option of ECN marking at an immediate (unsmoothed) shallow threshold to support use in data centres (see Section 5.2.7 of the FQ-CoDel spec [RFC8290]). In Linux, this has been modified so that the shallow threshold can be solely applied to ECT(1) packets [FQ_CoDel_Thresh]. Then, if there is a flow of Not-ECT or ECT(0) packets in the per-flow queue, the Classic AQM (e.g., CoDel) is applied; whereas, if there is a flow of ECT(1) packets in the queue, the shallower (typically sub-millisecond) threshold is applied. In addition, ECT(0) and Not-ECT packets could potentially be classified into a separate flow queue from ECT(1) and CE packets to avoid them mixing if they share a common flow identifier (e.g., in a VPN)."

I think we should refer to the above, and add relevant commentary. I'm happy to write a PR to do this. We also have the interesting design choice about having separate FQs for ECT(1). The aforementioned VPNs are one reason to do this. The other (possibly more common) reason is for hash collisions.

Section 5 Experiments

If we're going to list suggestions for experimentation, we could add:
* Assessment of performance differences of handling mixed L4S/Classic traffic through FQ-PIE vs DualPI2.
* Assessment of performance differences of FQ-PIE vs FQ-Codel, using and extending the hackathon work.

issues.title: Suggestions from Chris - July 22 (IETF 126)
issues.author: mohittahiliani
issues.body:
Mailing list thread: https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/tsvwg/eLoQszjTN7hzSLV81Jui_nbYFHc/

I've re-read the draft. In section 4 I'm happy with the new wording "maintains a target queue delay (such as the 15 ms default in [RFC8033])" . This conveys that people are empowered to choose a different target if they want. If I recall correctly, in your recent testing you achieved good performance with a 5ms target. Obviously variability of the bottleneck bandwidth is a major factor in choosing the target, but we don't necessarily need to go into that here.

A bit later down in section 4.1 we have a similar issue of a default being conveyed as set in stone:
"This drop probability is updated periodically (every 15 ms, as per [RFC8033])"

RFC8033 actually says "The update interval, T_UPDATE, is defaulted to be 15 milliseconds."

So I suggest we correct that.

Once done, there is some duplication lower down:
'It is important to note that the timestamping approach provides a "per-packet queue delay," while the drop probability is calculated periodically (every 15 ms, as specified in [RFC8033]).'
If you simply delete the part in brackets, then the above sentence is good in my eyes.

I would like to propose new wording for section 4.3, ECN Support. It currently says:

"FQ-PIE MAY support ECN by marking ECN-Capable Transport (ECT) packets [RFC3168] instead of dropping them, in accordance with the recommendations in Section 5.1 of [RFC8033]. The Linux, FreeBSD and ns-3 implementations of FQ-PIE comply with these recommendations at the time of writing this document."

I suggest replacing it with:

"FQ-PIE MAY support classic ECN [RFC3168] by marking ECT(0) packets as CE instead of dropping them, in accordance with the recommendations in Section 5.1 of [RFC8033]. The Linux, FreeBSD and ns-3 implementations of FQ-PIE comply with these recommendations at the time of writing this document.

A future implementation of FQ-PIE MAY support L4S [RFC9330] but such a design is not described by this document."

issues.title: Update the publication date of [FREEBSD-FQ-PIE]
issues.author: mohittahiliani
issues.body:
Thanks to Grenville Armitage!

The publication date of [FREEBSD-FQ-PIE] should be April 2016 rather than October 2016.

pulls.title: Minor rewording suggestions
pulls.author: Kevsy
pulls.body:
This PR includes two commits:

https://github.com/mohittahiliani/draft-ietf-tsvwg-fq-pie/pull/4/changes/8c764c93801af22eb4e25c5862b5514e10e937dc : Rephrasing of how the bucket approach differs

At least in plain language (I'm not a subject matter expert here)  this sentence appears confusing:

"While the goal of flow queuing is to assign a unique queue to each flow, flows can instead be hashed into a set of buckets using a hash function, where each bucket corresponds to its own queue."

"each bucket corresponds to its own queue." appears to meet the goal "to assign a unique queue to each flow". But the use of 'while' and 'instead' implies that the use of buckets corresponding to their own queues is at odds with the goal. So suggesting this rephrasing, *if my understanding is correct*

Alternatively, if the nuance is that the bucket corresponds to its own queue, but is decoupled from the queue in a way that 'regular' flow queuing is not, then that should be the stress of the sentence.

https://github.com/mohittahiliani/draft-ietf-tsvwg-fq-pie/pull/4/changes/7d7e907e26b11f793c3834f288554f332fa137b3 Minor grammar nit

I believe the colon better indicates that the explanation follows immediately below - otherwise the reader may not be sure at which later point the explanation is given.

Many thanks for the draft!

comments.author: mohittahiliani
comments.body:
Thanks for taking out time to read the document, and suggesting changes @Kevsy!

I will go through this PR over this weekend and get back to you.

comments.author: mohittahiliani
comments.body: I have merged these changes in https://github.com/mohittahiliani/draft-ietf-tsvwg-fq-pie/commit/7682e8bc1aa0a2fb735a3b50abe04edfa7149729, thanks @Kevsy for the suggestions and feedback on the document!

Thanks for initiating this!

The flow queuing has following points:

- The intention is to give each flow its own queue.
- Hashing is an approximation of this ideal.

Do you think this statement would make it more clear "While the goal of flow queuing is to assign a unique queue to each flow, a hashing-based scheme is used in practice, where flows are hashed into a set of buckets, each of which has its own queue."
Thanks @mohittahiliani - yes, I think your wording above makes it more clear 👍
